source_name: U.S. Census Bureau, Frequently Occurring Surnames from the 2010 Census (Comenetz, 2016); 'Names_2010Census_Top1000.xlsx' / full file of 162,253 surnames occurring 100+ times
license: U.S. Government work / PUBLIC DOMAIN (17 U.S.C. 105). Census Bureau aggregate genealogy/surname files contain only name frequencies (no individuals). Free to reuse and redistribute.
redistribution_notes: SHIPPABLE in-repo. This is the canonical, fully public-domain surname-frequency reference. Counts above are the published 2010-Census counts for the top 20 surnames (e.g. Smith 2,442,977; verified headline). prob = count / 294,979,716 where 294,979,716 is the Census-stated total of people whose surname was recorded and tabulated in the 2010 file (the surname-file universe, NOT the full 308.7M 2010 population). The tail bucket is the residual (all surnames ranked 21+). The official file also publishes a 'prop100k' column (occurrences per 100,000) and 'pctwhite/pctblack/...'; download the full Top1000 / 162k file to ship beyond the top 20. prob values here are agent-computed from count/universe and round to the published per-100k (Smith 828.19/100k = 0.008282) — consistent.
granularity_notes: National, surnames occurring 100+ times (162,253 names = ~90% of recorded surnames; top 1000 in a ready Excel). No geographic or age cross-tab. Strong, well-behaved QI marginal. This is the gold-standard redistributable name table.
